chunks: Ali b. al-Husayn b. Shaqir b. Ya'qub b. al-Harith b. Ibrahim al-Hamadani narrated to us in his house in Kufa. He said: Abu Abdillah Ja'far b. Ahmad b. Yusuf al-Azdi narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Bazraj al-Hannat narrated to us. He said: Amr b. al-Yasa' narrated to us from Shu'ayb al-Haddad. He said: I heard al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad, peace be upon him, saying:

"Surely, our narrations are difficult and distressing. None can handle them except an angel brought near, a commissioned prophet, a believer whose heart has been tested by Allah for faith, or a fortified city."
Amr said: So I said to Shu'ayb: "O Abu'l Hasan! What is the fortified city?" He said: I asked al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, about it, and he said to me: "The well-constituted heart."

key_terms.الْقَلْبُ الْمُجْتَمِعُ: the well-constituted heart - A heart unified in devotion and certainty
key_terms.صَعْبٌ مُسْتَصْعَبٌ: difficult and distressing - Describing the esoteric depth of the Imams' narrations
key_terms.مَدِينَةٌ حَصِينَةٌ: a fortified city - Metaphor for a heart impervious to doubt
key_terms.مَلَكٌ مُقَرَّبٌ: an angel brought near - Highest rank of angels closest to God

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq mean by 'our narrations are difficult and distressing'?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (as) reveals the esoteric nature of the Imams' teachings. The saying 'our narrations are difficult and distressing' became a famous maxim in Shia hadith literature, emphasizing that the knowledge of the Ahl al-Bayt requires spiritual preparation. The Imam lists four categories capable of bearing this knowledge: angels, prophets, believers whose hearts Allah has tested, and 'a fortified city.' When asked about this last metaphor, the Imam explains it means 'the well-constituted heart' -- one that is unified in its devotion and free from doubt.
